title: Get the whole SoC working for the desk: four cores, CPU and GPU frequency scaling
blocker: On 2026-11-02 the Qt desk (Stage Console) ran slowly on the tablet. Measured on the tablet: raising the Mali from 148.5 to 297 MHz at runtime (an out-of-tree `clk_set_rate` module, `~/gpuclk` in the VM) changed nothing (median frame 35 ms before, 38 ms after). Each frame instead spends 15-45 ms in `swap`, and a tab switch spends 150-260 ms in `sync` on the CPU. The CPU is the limit: the running v97 boots with `nosmp` in the DTB bootargs, a leftover from the v53 diagnostic build, so 1 of 4 Cortex-A7 cores is online, at 600 MHz with `CONFIG_CPU_FREQ` off, while the SoC reaches 1.2 GHz. The vendor CPU OPPs are 600/696 MHz at 1.15 V, 816 MHz at 1.2 V, 1008 MHz at 1.325 V and 1200 MHz at 1.425 V on DCDC1 `vdd_arm`; the GPU's are on DCDC2 `vdd_logic`. A RAM-only test, kexec (2.0.32, static, in `/data/kexec`) of the same kernel, DTB (`/sys/firmware/fdt`) and v97 ramdisk with only `nosmp` removed, did not come back on the network within 3 minutes. A second kexec the same night, with `nosmp` kept, did not come back on the network either, so kexec itself, not SMP, is what fails on this board (the first `kexec -e`, backgrounded inside the ssh session, died with it; `setsid` is needed). The owner saw the screen frozen, so the board hangs in kexec itself, not only the network; kexec is not a usable way to try kernels here. Then, with the owner's go, `nosmp` was found in the kernel's `CONFIG_CMDLINE`, not in the DTB. A v97 image with only that kernel rebuilt without it (`taq102-v97-smp.img`, sha256 791c13ea2250fc83..., also in `/data/kexec`; a control repack reproduces v97 byte for byte) was written to `boot` (raw LBA 139264, readback verified). The BCB (raw LBA 32800) held `boot-recovery`, so the tablet normally boots `recovery`, not `boot` as the README says; it was backed up to `/data/kexec/bcb-20261102.bin` and zeroed. The reboot into `boot` hung with a black screen. Likely cause: mainline `rk3128.dtsi` brings the secondaries up with `enable-method = "rockchip,rk3036-smp"`, poking registers the trust firmware owns, while the vendor DTB declares `psci { compatible = "arm,psci-1.0"; method = "smc"; }`. Recovered the same night: the screen stayed black whatever the owner pressed, but holding both buttons had put the board in loader mode (`rkdeveloptool ld`: `2207:310d Loader`), so `tools/flash-boot.sh` wrote v97 back to `boot` over USB (readback sha256 6dba4c17...) and it booted in 12 s. `boot` and `recovery` both hold v97 and the BCB stays zeroed, as this README describes; the desk at HEAD was reinstalled from `/data/desk-head`, and the VM tree's `.config` and `zImage` were put back from the `.sep9` copies. A black screen after a bad `boot` therefore still has a way back: hold both buttons and check `rkdeveloptool ld` from the Mac. On 2026-11-03 that trial turned out not to test SMP at all: the kernel inside `taq102-v97-smp.img` was cut to 9797632 of the 10331200 bytes its zImage header declares (its gzip stream never ends), while `~/zImage.smp` in the VM is whole (decompresses to 26986572 bytes, the same as v86, command line without `nosmp`). `tools/make-recovery.sh` now refuses such a kernel (`tools/check-zimage.py`, end - start against the file size). Two trial images are ready in the gate3-build folder, nothing flashed, both on the v99 ramdisk (dmxdesk v0.1.11) with the whole SMP kernel `zImage-7.3.0-rc2-v86-smp` (`083febb5…`): `boot-taq102-v99-smp-psci-trial.img` (SHA256 `45da72c666999f489c35ac9b1d30991d7d8cf1098ec36e91366aebe08dbc939b`), whose `second-v99-psci` carries `rk3126-taq102-v99-psci.dtb`, v88's DTB with exactly two changes (no `enable-method` on `cpus`, and `psci { compatible = "arm,psci-1.0"; method = "smc"; }` as in the vendor tree; `CONFIG_ARM_PSCI=y`), and `boot-taq102-v99-smp-rk3036-trial.img` (`45083823cff60b5934d6061117a4d3782a4a87b66ad47207107c27705316d03e`), the same kernel with v88's unchanged `second`, to tell the enable-method from SMP itself if PSCI fails. Both rebuild byte for byte; a control repack with the v86 kernel reproduces v99. Same night, done (the owner handed the tablet over for good): `tools/flash-boot.sh boot-taq102-v99-smp-psci-trial.img` (readback matched), and the tablet came back on the network in about 8 s with `psci: Using standard PSCI v0.2 function IDs`, `smp: Brought up 1 node, 4 CPUs`, `/sys/devices/system/cpu/online` 0-3, the desk linked (158 of 152 controls) and Wi-Fi associated; three minutes of four `bc` loops at 97% user CPU left it up with nothing new in dmesg (the `timer@2004404x` -22 lines were there on the first mainline boot too). Two runs of the Qt `taps/drive.sh` (current `/data/qt-full/qml`): 124-125 frames, p90 frame 40-41 ms, p90 sync 5-6 ms, against 113-115, 46-47 and 10 on one core; the median stays at 35 ms, mostly `swap`. `boot` now holds the PSCI image; `recovery` keeps single-core v99 as the fallback, and the BCB stays zeroed. The board DTS (`kernel/mainline/rk3126-taq102.dts`) carries the change, and built in the VM tree it gives the tested DTB (sorted dtc output identical); `taq102-mainline.config` drops `nosmp`. Later the same night, at runtime: vdd_arm and vdd_logic read 1.1 V (RK816 VSEL 0x1f); raising vdd_arm to 1.2 V by i2c and armclk to 816 MHz (`~/armclk` module in the VM) cut a `bc` job from 14.02 to 10.2 s, and with the Mali at 297 MHz (`~/gpuclk`) the Qt drive gave 156-159 frames, median 26 ms, p90 34-35 ms (four cores at 600 MHz and Mali 297: 146-149, 27-28, 36; Mali alone is the big step). The first `reboot-loader` under that `arm,psci-1.0` image (to write `boot-taq102-v100-smp-gpu297.img`) never reached loader mode or the network, and the owner power-cycled the board. A `psci-1.0` node makes PSCI the restart handler (priority 129, over the CRU's 128) and `pm_power_off`, and this firmware reports PSCI v65535.65535. The board DTS now declares `arm,psci` (v0.1) with only `cpu_off = <0x84000002>` and `cpu_on = <0x84000003>`, plus `assigned-clock-rates = <297000000>` on `&gpu`. On 2026-11-03 at 11:10 `boot-taq102-v101-smp-psci01-gpu297.img` (SHA256 `869e84eb…`) was written to `boot` from the running system (`dd` to raw LBA 139264, readback matched) and started by the CRU global reset (`devmem 0x20000100 32 0xfdb9`), which skips PSCI: `Using PSCI v0.1 Function IDs from DT`, four cores, `aclk_gpu` 297 MHz. Three plain `reboot`s came back in about 16 s each, and `reboot-loader` reached loader mode (`2207:310d`) and `rkdeveloptool rd` booted it again, all with four cores and the Mali at 297 MHz. `recovery` still holds single-core v99. A ramoops copied by `/init` at 5.5 s is the current boot's own live buffer, not the previous boot's; pstore was empty after the power cycle. Then CPU frequency. The cores still run at the bootloader's 600 MHz: describe DCDC1/DCDC2 in the DTS, give `cpu0` its `cpu-supply`, enable cpufreq-dt, and restore the GPU OPPs with `mali-supply`. A fixed 816 MHz without regulators does not work: rk3128.dtsi's own OPP gives 816 MHz at 1.075 V and vdd_arm reads 1.1 V, but on 2026-11-04 a ten-minute soak at 816 MHz (`armclk.ko`, four workers md5summing a 24 MB tmpfs blob against a reference) gave 2 wrong sums in 4356 runs, and the same soak at 600 MHz 0 in 3352. So the vendor's 1.2 V at 816 MHz is needed, and the rate must wait for the regulators; the earlier 816 MHz Qt numbers were taken with vdd_arm raised to 1.2 V by hand. `boot-taq102-v102-smp-cpu816-UNSTABLE-do-not-flash.img` (`b829c1ee…`, the v101 image with ARMCLK assigned 816 MHz on `&cru`) was built and never flashed; the DTS change was reverted. Mainline rk3128 has no tsadc node either, so nothing would throttle a faster rate. On 2026-11-04 v103 (RK816 rails, cpufreq-dt with schedutil, GPU devfreq on `vdd_logic`, Qt desk default) did not come back after `reboot`, and after a power cycle the two-button loader entry showed no USB device on the mini (`docs/journal.md`). Blocked: later on 2026-11-04 the panel stayed black and the owner's two-button entry, with the usual cable, brought no USB device of any kind to the mini and nothing on the LAN: the board does not respond at all. The PMIC stays powered from the battery through a power-off, so anything v103 wrote to the RK816 (the BUCK1/2 ramp field in its CONFIG registers, the bucks' voltages) survives it; only a battery disconnect resets it. Next, physical: leave it on a wall charger for an hour and retry the buttons; if still dead, open the case and unplug the battery for a minute, which resets the RK816; then loader mode and `tools/flash-boot.sh` with v101. Next: put v101 back, touch `/data/taq102-use-c-desk`, then boot `boot-taq102-v104a-cpufreq-userspace.img` (rails and cpufreq with the `userspace` governor, GPU fixed) and step the CPU through the OPPs by hand with an md5 soak at each, reading `vdd_arm` back over i2c. The board DTS, `taq102-app`, `taq102-qt-desk` and `tools/make-desk-ramdisk.sh` changes are in the working tree, not committed, until a boot proves them.
